newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps sluggish, gasoline pressured lower.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps sluggish, gasoline pressured lower.

text.p: European oil swaps faced a slow day on Tuesday after the long holiday weekend in the U.K.
"Today is the fourth day of the weekend and levels are carrying on from last week," said one trader.

Gasoline was one of the complex's few movers, heading downwards on Tuesday. Pressure from easier NYMEX gasoline and the day's late sell-off in crude helped push May gasoline swaps down to $192.75-$193.75 with June $1.50 off this level.
Trades were heard earlier in the day at $194, $193.50 and $193.00 before easing down lower.

No Brent CFDs were heard concluded, but levels firmed slightly to -29 cents on May 6-9, with May 12-16 at $22.50. Monthly CFDs against the IPE were steady from Friday with the balance of May at 32 cents under the front line Brent contract with forward levels at -26 cents June, -21 cents July, -17 cents 3Q and -13 cents 4Q97.
Low sulphur fuel oil cargo swaps showed a slight recovery during the course of the day with $87 and then $88 done for balance of May while June was concluded at $90.25.
High sulphur barge swaps traded at $83.25 twice for May and at $83.75 for June and $86 on 3Q.
Gas oil futures closed $1.00 a tonne stronger, reclaiming some of last week's sharp losses when the May contract lost $5.50.
Activity was sparse with buyers and sellers wide apart under little pressure to conclude traders, dealers said.
"The gap is as wide as a bus with bids at +3 and offers at +$6," one said.
Gas oil crack spreads were steady with 3Q around $4.30 a barrel for 4Q with 1Q 98 hovering close to $4.65 and 2Q 98 around $4.10.
